claims.summary: Likely Snag: first_word_after (L89) split_whitespace + trim_matches may mishandle complex punctuation / non-standard whitespace, or capture only the first token when a multi-word phrase is the relation; greedy longest_exact_known_model_control_marker_at (L97) could misalign the remainder for overlapping same-length markers.
claims.disposition: verified_existing. first_word_after trims non-alnum/_ and skips empties; punctuation/colon/adverb/emphasis skipping is pinned by tests L2670/L2724/L2771/L2943 and unicode-alnum grouping by L2112. By design ONLY the first finite token is the relation (pinned L2640) — a multi-word phrase is intended to reduce to its first verb, not a bug. Greedy match = max_by_key(len) L106, single-pass, no second-order marker creation (accounting_basis L507). No misbehavior at the report SHA.

claims.summary: Test 1 (Reference Syntax): a marker in non-standard brackets like 「[MARKER]」 should make exact_reference_delimiter_syntax (L199) identify the GroupedExactKnownToken context.
claims.disposition: verified_existing. Context is decided by the innermost delimiter (before.first()/after.first(), L215); [ ] -> Grouped (L177/L193). For 「[MARKER]」 the inner [ ] yields Grouped and the outer 「」 adds one depth level -> depth 2. The same code path is verified at depth 3/4 by grouped-under-outer-quote tests L2418 (﹁《（…）》﹂) and L2195 ("“【([…])】”"), ASCII bracket grouped L2153, CJK quote L2382. The exact 「[…]」 bytes are not verbatim-pinned but are mechanically determined by verified components (no depth-specific branch exists).

claims.summary: Test 2 (Relation Verb): [MARKER] behaves like a ghost should make followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation (L64) identify 'behaves' as the relation, keeping the marker visible in the remainder.
claims.disposition: verified_existing with plain correction (not domesticated): for a BRACKETED marker the delimiter path is checked FIRST (reference_syntax L49-52), so [ ] short-circuits to Grouped and the relation fn is never consulted — the marker stays visible via GROUPING, not relation. The relation path her test names is exercised and tested only for a BARE marker: 'behaves as'/'behaves like' -> explicit_relation_occurrences=1 (L2548). Both poles are covered: grouped L2153, bare-behaves relation L2548; the bracket-short-circuits-relation nuance is noted at L2680.
